observations: The required wrapper selected the booted iOS 26 compact iPhone and both HabitDetailUITests passed.

The run produced the six requested owner-journey attachments plus both requested accessibility Dynamic Type attachments; inactive-after-archive was exported temporarily but intentionally not committed.
The UDID was the first available iOS 26 iPad returned by the required simctl JSON traversal.
Both tests passed with explicit readable-column bounds, no-split-group, hidden-shell-tab, hit-region, semantic, mutation, persistence, and Dynamic Type assertions.

simctl ui in Xcode 26.6 does not expose a Reduce Motion option; the simulator preference com.apple.Accessibility ReduceMotionEnabled was set to 1 through simctl spawn and read back as 1 before launch.
The test exercised Back, previous/next month selection, period callout open/dismiss, Edit cancel, Edit save, entry deletion, Archive, and Reactivate while ReduceMotionEnabled was 1.

Both temporary Dynamic Type attachments were visually inspected: despite dark system preference, the app remained visibly forced-light with the #F7F2E7 Almanac paper surface and light system status chrome.
After capture, appearance was restored to light, content size to large, and ReduceMotionEnabled was restored to 0.

elementDetection.reason: The detail is a ScrollView with intentionally offscreen content. Every actionable offscreen target is explicitly scrolled into a hittable position and asserted instead.

directlyMeasured: every real daily period while scrolling
semanticObservations: Title and metadata expose complete, untruncated labels at default, Accessibility Large, and Accessibility Extra Large.
Month buttons expose Previous month or Next month labels plus the displayed month as their accessibility value.
Streak facts expose complete Current streak and Best streak labels with localized units.
History buttons expose full date/range, state, standing, and progress; selected periods expose the selected trait and their default action opens or dismisses the matching callout.
Entry deletion controls expose full date, time, amount, and Delete entry labels plus a default button action.
Roster lifecycle alternatives are available without swipe through context-menu buttons and named accessibility actions Edit, Archive or Reactivate, Delete, and conditional Retry streak.

observations: Pencil MCP structural inspection found no clipped/collapsed nodes and no effects on the Habit Detail board.

Final screenshots match the paper chrome, uniform serif screen title, muted metadata, balanced default CURRENT/BEST pair, vertical accessibility adaptation, quiet ochre risk, month controls, 44-point garden, approved fills/strokes, centered legend, flat hairline entries, and quiet lifecycle action.
No final screenshot shows a shadow, alarm-red treatment, native Form chrome, iPad sidebar, split view, or floating tab pill.
The iPad screenshots visibly keep the content in a centered readable column and clear the top and bottom safe areas.

The Pencil board viewport ends after the legend; recent entries and lifecycle continuation were compared against the same approved variables, spacing, flat-surface language, and implementation tokens rather than literal entry/lifecycle nodes in KytOH.

red.completeIssueDescription: Contrast is not high enough for SwiftUI.AccessibilityNode unless font size is larger.

redGreenDefect.fix: HabitDetailView uses the existing semantic AlmanacPalette.inkMuted token for the active Archive habit label; Reactivate remains moss. No global palette or unrelated surface changed.

limitations.observation: No physical iOS device was connected and reliable simulator VoiceOver traversal was not driven. This evidence does not claim traversal order, spoken cadence, rotor behavior, or physical-device VoiceOver usability.
limitations.automatedBoundary: XCTest verified complete labels, values, selected traits, default actions, named non-swipe actions, Apple accessibility audits, and 44-point hit regions.
limitations.humanFollowUp: A human must traverse the complete detail journey with VoiceOver on a physical iPhone and iPad before any manual accessibility criterion is attested.

limitations.observation: The approved production detail surface has no deterministic operation-failure UI seam. No fixture-controlled production failure was added and no retry screenshot was fabricated.
limitations.automatedBoundary: The adaptive UI test measures and enables any Try again control if one is present; HabitDetailModelTests cover deterministic delete/archive/reactivate retry behavior.
limitations.humanFollowUp: Capture a real operation failure only when a supported deterministic production or test seam exists.

limitations.observation: The approved KytOH Habit Detail Pencil board ends after the legend and contains no literal Recent entries or lifecycle nodes.
limitations.comparisonBoundary: Final entry and lifecycle screenshots were compared to the board variables and visual language, and their behavior/accessibility was tested directly; no claim is made that those continuation nodes exist in Pencil.
